The chapter on Storytelling for Elders is largely Storyteller-facing advice on running an all-elder chronicle or integrating elder characters into an existing one (chronicle scale, scope, theme, plot construction, troubleshooting disruptive players). That material is narrative craft rather than game data and isn't reproduced here. Two pieces of it, however, are concrete character-advancement rules that affect elder characters directly, and are collected below.

Elder Experience Costs

Elders are the guardians of the status quo, and change comes to them more slowly — the older a Kindred, the more Experience it costs to learn something new. Storytellers running elder characters should use the character's chronological age to determine the Experience cost of new Traits, Abilities, Disciplines and the removal of Negative Traits, rather than the standard costs.

Time-Lapse Advancement

In chronicles designed to span decades or longer (for example, beginning in the Enlightenment and continuing to the present night), characters may achieve elder status simply by surviving. Two methods handle the transition:

  • Method One: Start characters as neonates. At the end of each session representing a transition into the next era, award each character a number of Experience Traits to spend however they wish during the transition.
  • Method Two: As Method One, but restrict spending during the transition primarily to Traits and capabilities the character actually used successfully during the preceding portion of the chronicle.

Pretenders

Pretenders are vampires elder in generation but not necessarily in age — Kindred recently Embraced by a powerful sire, or diablerists who have stolen an elder's power. True elders grudgingly admit Pretenders into elder society out of respect for the potency of their vitae, not respect for the individual.

Characters created as Pretenders use the standard character creation system, with the following modifications:

  • Pretenders start at 10th Generation, and may lower their generation further with Negative Traits. No Pretender may start below 8th Generation.
  • Pretenders receive the additional @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.rules-reference.JournalEntry.St7uVm2DqK4nRy8X]{Status} Trait Known.
  • All Pretenders are automatically one Trait down in any Social Challenge against a true elder.
  • Pretenders should expect some degree of animosity from true elders: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} Kindred generally limit this to social sniping about the character's age, while @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} vampires may express it in far uglier ways.
